correctness.rationale: The repaired result retains the nonempty-word convention and proves ranks 3,4,5. A map commutes exactly when it sends blocks to blocks and representatives to representatives; mapping a positive block to zero forces its one bit to vanish, and multiplication multiplies the transmitted bits. The specified adjacent transposition and full cycle generate the units for b>=3; at b=1 the identity is included explicitly. Unit conjugates of t,z,c give single zero deletions, selective bit deletions and positive collapses. For an index map moving zero to a>0, the three cases are an existing positive source of a, an existing source of zero, or a positive collision to vacate a block before the swap. These realize every maximal-bit map and bit deletions give the rest. A nonempty unit word can use only units. A word for t requires an index permutation moving zero, and a word for z needs a factor moving zero while restricting to a full-bit positive permutation. These two needed types are distinct even at b=1. For c the first merger must act noninjectively on the entire set of positive indices, while preserving their bits and avoiding zero. It is neither of the other two types.
residual_risks: The reproduction tests all point-map commutants only at b=1,2; at b=3,4 it checks commuting generators and the closure size against the proved count.
The finite calculations do not establish the unbounded theorem. The rank at b=1 is 2 only under the alternative empty-word convention.

value.rationale: One singleton changes the compositional constraints in an otherwise uniform doubleton family. Giving a minimal generating set and proving the need for three different nonunit mechanisms determines an exact natural mixed case of the regular centralizer rank problem. This is useful independently of the elementary counting formula and the b=1 convention correction.
